As committee is aware, the city's multi-year business plan and budget cycle began with the
intentions of transitioning to a four-year budget cycle to coincide with the election and
provided tool to provide more certainty and transparency to residents as well as improving
internally efficiencies.
A two-year cycle was originally introduced in 2020-2021 as the first steps toward this implementation.
Then again, in 2021, another two-year cycle was approved due to the uncertainties of the COVID
pandemic and a two-year budget, including 2022 and 2023, was approved.
These two budget cycles have given the administration a time to reflect on the challenges and successes
of multi-year budgeting.
As outlined in the report, a budget cycle of more than two years presents many challenges
including a higher degree of risk in future assumptions.
While reviewing other four-year budget cycles and other major Western Canadian cities, it was
evident that significant adjustments were made during mid-cycle reviews that essentially
required duplication of work and the loss of the intended efficiencies.
The city's experience with the two-year budget cycle to date has brought many efficiencies
to the organization, most importantly, allowing an off-cycle year to allow administration
to focus on the work that needs to be done as a growing and evolving city rather than continuously
budgeting.
This has saved thousands of hours of administrative time in those off-cycle years.
The administration believes that moving to a four-year cycle would actually be a slight step backwards
for these efficiencies as it would not only take more time to do the upfront forecast, but
it also requires significant adjustments mid-cycle that would be near equivalent to rebuilding
the budget.
In regards to transparency, while the four-year forecast does provide a longer horizon, as we've
seen examples from other cities, the majority of the time these priorities and budgets significantly
change requiring that extensive rework.
The recommendation in the report are for the administration to proceed with adjustments to the
multi-year business plan and budget process to adopt a two-year cycle moving forward.
If approved, the administration will report back with an updated policy to reflect such.
